problem:
The cubic polynomial $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-2,{x}_{2,3}=\pm 4\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $3.$ Find $f(x).$

$f(x)=$
{{field-1}}${x}^{3}\,+$
{{field-2}}${x}^{2}\,+$
{{field-3}}$x\,+$
{{field-4}}
worked_solution:
Since $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-2$ and ${x}_{2,3}=\pm 4\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=3,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =3(x-(-2))(x-4\text{i})(x-(-4\text{i})) \\  & =3(x+2)(x-4\text{i})(x+4\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3(x+2)(x-4\text{i})(x+4\text{i}) & = \\ 3(x+2)({x}^{2}-(4\text{i})^{2}) & = \\ 3(x+2)({x}^{2}+16) & = \\ 3({x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+16x+32) & = \\ 3{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+48x+96 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=3{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+48x+96.$
